map.考古地层识别对照，涵盖地质时代与中国主要考古学文化期特征，辅助遗址地层划分与年代: An archaeological stratum identification reference covering geologic ages and the characteristics of China's main archaeological cultural phases, supporting site stratigraphy and date assignment.
map.划分遗址地层时，按叠压—打破关系排列先后顺序：上层晚于下层，被打破的单位晚于打破: When dividing site strata, order them by superposition and truncation: upper layers are later than lower ones, and a truncated unit is later than the unit that truncates it.
map.结合地质时代与考古学文化期定位：如全新世地层多对应新石器及以后，更新世堆积多为旧: Position it by combining geologic age with archaeological cultural phase: Holocene strata mostly correspond to the Neolithic and later, while Pleistocene deposits are mostly Paleolithic; cultural phases are anchored by typical artifacts (stone industries, pottery).
map.记录生土/熟土界线：生土即未受人类活动扰动的天然堆积，其顶面往往是一个遗址人类活: Record the natural/cultivated stratum boundary: natural stratum is undisturbed natural deposit, and its top surface is often an important reference for the lower boundary of human activity at a site.
map.一组叠压关系定年: Dating a set of superposition relationships
map.：探方中第②层（耕土）叠压第③层（明清），第③层叠压第④层（宋元），第④层下见生: : in the test pit layer ② (plough soil) overlies layer ③ (Ming-Qing), which overlies layer ④ (Song-Yuan), and natural stratum appears below ④. By the lower-earlier principle ④ precedes ③ precedes ②; the Song-Yuan porcelain from ④ and the Ming-Qing blue-and-white from ③ corroborate each other, so the stratigraphic order matches the cultural phases.
map.地层学和类型学定年有什么区别？: What Is the Difference Between Stratigraphic and Typological Dating?
map.地层学依据堆积的上下叠压与打破关系定相对先后；类型学依据遗物形态演变定文化期先后: Stratigraphy orders layers by superposition and truncation; typology orders cultural phases by the evolution of artifact forms. The two cross-check each other: if typology shows earlier material in an upper layer, that usually means disturbance or later digging, so the stratigraphy must be re-examined.
map.什么是生土？为什么重要？: What Is Natural Stratum and Why Does It Matter?
map.生土是未经人类翻动的天然沉积（如冲积、坡积），其顶面标志着遗址人类活动的最早底界: Natural stratum is undisturbed natural sediment (alluvial, colluvial, and similar), and its top surface marks the earliest boundary of human activity at the site. Finding it means the test pit has been dug to the bottom of the deposit, which is the key basis for closing the pit.
